gloss: to skip out, ditch, bail on

definitions.gloss: to skip out on, ditch, bail on
definitions.explanation: To fail to show up for or abandon an obligation, often without notice or explanation.
To pretend not to know about something, especially to avoid responsibility.

examples.english: I skipped out on my part-time job.

examples.japanese: {授業|じゅぎょう}をバックレて{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I ditched class and went to hang out.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}をバックレるなよ。
{飲|の}み{会|かい}をバックレたら{怒|おこ}られた。
examples.english: I got scolded for ditching the drinking party.

examples.japanese: {聞|き}いてもバックレるつもりか。
examples.english: Are you going to play dumb even when I ask you?

examples.japanese: {知|し}らないふりしてバックレようとするな。

notes:
バックレる is youth slang derived from {白|しら}を{切|き}る (to play innocent) or バックれる (from "back" + verb ending). It's conjugated as a godan verb: バックレる、バックレない、バックレた.

This word has a negative connotation and implies irresponsibility. It's very casual and should not be used in formal situations.

Common collocations:
- バイトをバックレる: skip out on a part-time job
- {授業|じゅぎょう}をバックレる: ditch class
- {約束|やくそく}をバックレる: bail on plans
